What Is IAH? (And Why It Matters)

IAH stands for George Bush Intercontinental Airport, Houston's largest airport. Located about 23 miles north of downtown, it handles over 40 million passengers annually—making it one of the busiest airports in the country.

Price Surge = Shock at Checkout

During peak hours (mornings, evenings, holidays), surge pricing kicks in hard.

Real example:

You book thinking it'll be $30. By the time you're in the car, you've been charged $75+.

Drivers Cancel

Rideshare drivers see the airport fee and long distance, then cancel. You're left waiting 10+ minutes while they avoid your ride.

No Predictability

You get in a random car with a random driver. Some will be professional. Others... not so much.

No surge pricing. Ever.

You know the cost before booking. No surprises at checkout.

No cancellations. No delays. Just reliability.

title: Arrive in Style: Houston's Must-Attend Events Worth a Limo Ride
summary: From Rockets tip-off to Galveston galas, here's why pairing your next Houston event with a limo service turns a great night into an unforgettable one.
content:
Houston's event calendar stays packed year-round, and getting there should feel just as exciting as the occasion itself. Whether you're headed to a Houston Rockets game at the Toyota Center, a sold-out concert at the Shell Energy Stadium, or the annual Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo, a professional limo service transforms the entire experience from the curb up.

Skip the downtown parking shuffle and the surge-priced rideshare surge. Instead, step out of a sleek black sedan or stretch SUV right at the entrance while your driver handles the logistics. It's the same move made by Houston's pro athletes, visiting celebrities, and corporate executives rolling into the GRB Convention Center.

Planning a Quinceañera, wedding, or milestone birthday? Limos aren't just for red carpets anymore. Many Houston families now book SUVs and party buses for everything from Memorial Park picnics to wine tours through Fredericksburg. Add LED lighting, a stocked cooler, and a chauffeur who knows every shortcut through I-610 traffic, and you've got a mobile celebration before you even reach the venue.

Book early for major Houston weekends, especially during rodeo season, Final Four week, and Astros playoff runs, when demand spikes fast.

title: Rolling Into Forever: Why a Houston Limo Makes Your Wedding Day Unforgettable
summary: From the first curb-side photo to the final getaway, a Houston wedding limo turns logistics into luxury and gives your day the polished pace it deserves.
content:
Your wedding day moves fast, and the transportation you choose quietly sets the tone for nearly every moment in between. A professional Houston wedding limo does more than move you from ceremony to reception; it gives your timeline breathing room, your photographer stunning backdrops, and your guests a front-row sense that something special is happening.

Houston traffic can be unpredictable, especially with ceremony venues, photo locations, and reception halls scattered across the Galleria, Rice Village, The Heights, or downtown. An experienced chauffeur team plans the route in advance, builds in buffer time, and knows the shortcuts that keep the day on schedule without anyone in the wedding party having to check a map.

Inside the vehicle, the mood shifts. Parents relax, the bridal party pops champagne, and there is a calm stretch where everyone breathes before the next stop. Stretch sedans, classic Rolls-Royce styles, and luxury SUVs can be coordinated to match the size and style of your party.

Book early, especially during Houston's spring and fall wedding seasons, and ask about red-carpet service, "Just Married" signage, and flexible hourly packages. The right limo company becomes a trusted partner, not just a vendor, and that peace of mind is worth every mile.

title: Houston Limo Travel Tips: Ride Like a Pro in Space City
summary: Make the most of your Houston limo experience with these insider travel tips, from booking smart to navigating the city's busy streets in style.
content:
Booking a limo in Houston can elevate any trip, but a few smart strategies help you get the most out of your ride. First, reserve early, especially during rodeo season, Astros home games, and major conventions at the George R. Brown. Houston traffic can be unpredictable, so build in extra buffer time, particularly when heading to IAH or Hobby airports during rush hour.

Always confirm pickup details the day before, including the exact curb location and your chauffeur's contact information. If you are traveling with a group, share the itinerary in advance so the driver can plan efficient routes through the Galleria, Midtown, or The Woodlands without unnecessary delays.

Pack light and keep essentials within reach, since cabin space in a limousine is best enjoyed without bulky luggage. Stay hydrated, especially during Houston's humid summer months, and use the complimentary Wi-Fi or charging ports to catch up on work between stops. Finally, tip your chauffeur 15 to 20 percent for excellent service. A little planning ensures your Houston limo ride feels effortless from curbside to destination.

title: Houston Limo Travel Tips: Make the Most of Your Ride
summary: Smart advice for booking and enjoying a limo ride in Houston, from choosing the right vehicle to navigating the city's busy highways.
content:
Houston's sprawling layout makes a limo one of the smartest ways to navigate the city in comfort and style. Whether you're heading to a Texans game, a wedding in The Heights, or a corporate event downtown, a few simple tips can elevate your experience.

First, book early—especially during rodeo season, playoff weekends, and major conventions at the George R. Brown Convention Center. Limousine availability drops fast, and last-minute reservations often come with premium pricing or limited vehicle options.

Next, match the vehicle to your occasion. A classic stretch sedan suits a romantic night out or airport transfer, while a stretch SUV or Hummer is ideal for bachelorette parties and birthday celebrations. For larger groups, consider a luxury Sprinter van that seats up to 14 passengers without sacrificing elegance.

Confirm your pickup details the day before. Houston traffic can be unpredictable, especially along I-610 and the Southwest Freeway during rush hour. A reputable chauffeur will monitor your flight or event timing and adjust accordingly, but clear communication helps everything run smoothly.

Finally, ask about hourly minimums, gratuity, and cancellation policies before you sign. Most reputable Houston limo companies include a standard 15–20% gratuity and require a two- to three-hour minimum. Knowing these details upfront prevents surprise charges and keeps your focus on enjoying the ride.

title: Why a Houston Limo Is the Wedding Day Upgrade Couples Keep Talking About

title: IAH vs Hobby: Which Houston Airport Should You Fly Into?
summary: A complete guide to Houston's two airports — amenities, locations, and which one makes sense for your trip.
content:
Houston is served by two major airports: George Bush Intercontinental (IAH) and William P. Hobby (HOU). Choosing the right one can save you time, money, and stress.

George Bush Intercontinental (IAH) is Houston's primary international airport, located about 23 miles north of downtown. It has five terminals and serves most major international carriers. IAH is the better choice for international flights, long-haul domestic routes, and if you're traveling to or from the north side of Houston (The Woodlands, Spring, Conroe).

William P. Hobby (HOU) is smaller, closer to downtown (about 7 miles), and primarily serves domestic routes via Southwest Airlines and a few other carriers. It's much easier to navigate with shorter security lines and quicker baggage claim. Hobby is ideal for short-haul domestic flights and if you're staying in downtown, Midtown, or the Medical Center.

Our recommendation: For international travel, fly into IAH. For domestic trips, especially with Southwest, Hobby is hard to beat. Either way, AvaLimo covers both airports with the same premium service — flight tracking included.
